items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: You know Mack Avenue Records, Gretchen Valade, Mack Avenue, she’s the heiress to the Carhartt fortune, the working clothes gear. And she loves jazz.

ctx.x: I think jazz, for the people that think jazz is dead, you know, good luck. No. I think jazz is healthier than it’s been maybe in the history of jazz. I think it probably is, as an entire ecosystem. But within that there are problems, and the streaming issue is a problem. Record companies who have millions and millions and millions of titles can now make a living off of streaming. Because they get one nth of a percent for every play, so they don’t care which title you play, they’ve got millions of them. But if…

Detroit. She gave another eight million, I think it might be up to ten or twelve million dollars now, to Wayne State University to build a jazz performance facility, it’s right outside of Detroit. But that’s a jazz angel.
